purpose: Track suspected or clinically-sensitive issues that must NOT be changed casually. The final visual/clinical result observed by the physician is considered CORRECT unless a real, reproduced, user-visible bug or a clear code-level defect proves otherwise. Tests exist to find software-engineering defects, not to redefine clinically accepted behavior.
changeOnlyWhen: a real reproduced user-visible bug proves the output is wrong
the physician confirms the current output is clinically incorrect
a clear double-operation / code-level contradiction that preserves the result accidentally but creates risk

issues.observation: After apply_k_flip_for_stack_order(n), display_k_to_raw_k(1) returns -1 (the test contract expects 0). The k-row translation appears double-offset (-2): __init__ sets M[2,3]=-1 (R30 1-based->0-based), then _k_flip_4x4 composes another -1. is_k_flip_active stays False (k22>0).
issues.whyMayBeWrong: A -1 offset applied twice could shift slice-index mapping by one. Looks like a possible double-operation (the principle's 'same offset applied twice') rather than a clean reversal or a clean 1-based offset.
issues.reasonForDeferral: Clinical slice-ordering. There is a genuine intent contradiction: the docstring says 'reverses the slice stack' while the tests AND the hardcoded log '[DISPLAY_K_RUNTIME_BIND] k_flip_active=False' say it is NOT a reversal. Crucially, the live viewer rendered the opened CT correctly (log: FAST:first_image_visible series=202 slice=78 of 156), so the final clinical output currently APPEARS CORRECT. Must not change without the R30 author's confirmed intent and a real-series slice-order check.
issues.risk: If another orientation/stack path changes later, the double-offset could surface as an off-by-one slice mapping.
issues.recommendedInvestigation: Confirm intent (reversal vs offset-only). Add a runtime log of display_k_to_raw_k(1)/(n) on a known axial CT; verify physician sees correct superior->inferior order. Only then adjust code OR tests.

issues.observation: 3 tests assert the pre-R30 (0-based, effective==raw) contract; the code is R30 (1-based display; effective differs from raw by the -1 k translation).
issues.whyMayBeWrong: Nothing in the CODE — it is the physician-verified R30 behavior. The TESTS are stale (assert the old contract).
issues.reasonForDeferral: Updating these is a test-only, behavior-preserving change but requires careful R30-derived recomputation of clinical geometry values; deferred to avoid asserting a wrong derived value. No code/behavior change is warranted.
issues.risk: low (tests only; code is correct).
issues.recommendedInvestigation: Update the 3 tests to the R30 contract (display k=1 -> raw k=0; effective = raw composed with the -1 k translation). Test-only.

issues.observation: After clearing a patient's DICOM files from Settings -> Viewer Configuration -> Information Storage, the home patient table kept showing the study as downloaded/green. The panel emitted storageChanged but nothing was connected to it.
issues.whyMayBeWrong: The table caches per-study download status; with no invalidation signal it served the stale (downloaded) badge even though the files were gone. Pure UI-status sync; download status itself is recomputed from disk (check_study_complete), so no clinical output is affected.
issues.reasonForDeferral: n/a - fixed. storageChanged is now connected (through the lazily-built viewer-config tab) to a focused patient_table_widget.refresh_download_statuses_local_only(), which clears the in-memory status cache and recomputes each visible row from disk WITHOUT any server call or refresh-button animation (smallest blast radius for a storage clear). A defensive fallback to the broader refresh_download_statuses() remains if the focused method is absent. The connect + handler are fully guarded so they cannot break startup or the existing modality-grid wiring.
issues.risk: low-medium (misleading downloaded/green badge after a clear; user might think data is still present).
issues.recommendedInvestigation: Live confirm: download a study (green), Clear Patient Data for it, verify the home badge flips to not-downloaded without restart.

issues.observation: There was no way to detect or repair DB/disk drift (DB marks a study downloaded but its files are missing; a series thumbnail_path points at a deleted file; a disk study folder has no DB record).
issues.whyMayBeWrong: Partial deletions or interrupted clears leave the DB and disk out of sync, which is exactly what produces a lingering green/downloaded badge. This is a data-integrity/maintenance feature, not a change to any rendered output.
issues.reasonForDeferral: n/a - fixed. Added a read-only validator (db_studies_missing_files, orphan_disk_studies, thumbnails_missing_source) and a conservative repair that removes stale DB study records (instances->series->studies, cascade-agnostic) and NULLs dangling thumbnail pointers. Repair NEVER deletes any files; orphan disk folders are reported only (could be a not-yet-indexed import). Exposed via a 'Check Consistency' button that offers repair only when repairable items exist.
issues.risk: low (read-only validate; repair is files-safe and DB-only).
issues.recommendedInvestigation: n/a

issues.observation: If file deletion succeeded but the matching DB cleanup failed (e.g. database locked), the action could report success while leaving the DB inconsistent (the partial-deletion confusion case).
issues.whyMayBeWrong: Silent partial success hides a real inconsistency from the user; the operation should report a warning and not claim full success.
issues.reasonForDeferral: n/a - fixed. CleanupResult now carries a warnings list; a DB-cleanup failure after files were removed sets success=False and surfaces a 'WARNING' message + the specific warning in the result dialog, so the user knows to run Check Consistency.
issues.risk: low (reporting/UX integrity).
issues.recommendedInvestigation: n/a

issues.observation: native_fault.log on the other PC (installed build) captured a Windows access violation with the live-event-loop stack 'animate_hover <- enterEvent <- notify <- run_forever'. animate_hover/animate_active created a LOCAL QPropertyAnimation(self, b'geometry') with no parent and no stored reference, called start(), and returned. Python could garbage-collect the wrapper while the 150-200 ms animation was still running, freeing the underlying C++ QObject mid-flight -> crash. Fast hovering across tabs (an impatient user) creates many short-lived animations and makes the race likely.
issues.whyMayBeWrong: Classic PySide6 lifetime defect (a running QPropertyAnimation must stay referenced/parented). Pure UI animation; no clinical geometry/slice-order/rendering involved.
issues.reasonForDeferral: n/a - fixed immediately (clear SE/stability defect, output-preserving).
issues.resolution: FIXED (2026-06-14): both animate_hover and animate_active now reuse ONE animation per widget, lazily created as QPropertyAnimation(self, b'geometry', self) (parented to self) and stored on self._hover_animation / self._active_animation (kept reference), stopped before each restart. It can no longer be GC'd while running, and reusing one instance avoids accumulating child objects. Same duration/easing/geometry deltas -> identical visible animation. The two OTHER access violations in native_fault.log (main.py:1597 and :1606) are shutdown/takeover teardown (known, mostly benign).
issues.risk: medium (intermittent hard crash during normal tab hovering).
issues.relatedStudy: native_fault.log 'Current thread ... animate_hover ... run_forever' (other PC, installed build)
issues.recommendedInvestigation: Reaches the other PC only after a rebuilt installer (it runs the frozen build). The same bare-local QPropertyAnimation pattern exists in a few non-crash paths (app_handler fade-out, _hp_layout opacity, thumbnail_manager border) — lower risk (fade/opacity, often on widgets being destroyed) but worth the same parent+reference treatment opportunistically.

issues.observation: download_diagnostics.log on the other PC has ~337 ERROR lines, dominated by network connectivity to the PACS server: 45x NetworkError 'Too many broadcast messages, no response received', '[WinError 10060] connection attempt failed ... party did not properly respond' (TCP timeout), 3x 'Connection lost while receiving data', plus 1x UnicodeDecodeError and 1x JSONDecodeError on a desynced/garbled response. app.log and db_diagnostics.log are clean over the same period.
issues.whyMayBeWrong: These are server/network conditions on the other PC (host unreachable / slow / dropping connections), not a client logic defect. The client logs them and retries; the app stayed up (clean app.log/db). NOT something to 'fix' in code.
issues.reasonForDeferral: Environmental — verify the other PC's connectivity to the PACS server (firewall, host up, correct host/port, link quality). One genuine client-robustness sub-item: a desynced response currently surfaces as UnicodeDecodeError/JSONDecodeError instead of the structured 'Response too large' desync path — a candidate for more graceful handling (already partially guarded for GetSeriesImages).
issues.risk: low (client-side; the failures are handled/retried). User-facing impact is failed/slow downloads when the server link is bad.
issues.recommendedInvestigation: Confirm network/server health on the other PC. Optionally harden the recv/decode path so a garbled response always maps to the structured desync error + bounded retry rather than a raw UnicodeDecodeError/JSONDecodeError.

issues.observation: pc2 (previous installed build) native_fault.log: access violation with stack '_hp_layout.py _hide_loading_overlay <- hide_loading <- _on_patient_double_clicked_async'. The overlay fade built a QPropertyAnimation on the overlay's graphics effect WITHOUT a liveness check; during an async patient-open teardown race (frequent on that PC because of network failures) the overlay's C++ object was already gone, so effect.opacity()/the animation dereferenced a deleted QObject -> crash, which the main.py notify() override escalates into a hard process crash.
issues.whyMayBeWrong: Missing liveness guard on a UI-teardown race. Pure UI overlay animation; no clinical geometry/slice-order/rendering involved. The sibling components/loading_overlay.py was already hardened the same way; _hp_layout was not.
issues.reasonForDeferral: n/a - fixed (clear SE/stability defect, output-preserving). Current source was still exposed (the guard existed only in loading_overlay.py).
issues.resolution: FIXED (2026-06-15): both methods now verify shiboken6.isValid(overlay) and wrap the fade in try/except, falling back to overlay.hide() so a dying overlay can never raise into the patient-open path. Reference still kept on self._loading_overlay_anim. Matches the loading_overlay.py pattern.
issues.risk: medium (intermittent hard crash on patient open, worse under flaky network).
issues.relatedStudy: pc2 native_fault.log crash @ _hide_loading_overlay; coincident WinError 10060/10065 in the same open
issues.recommendedInvestigation: Reaches pc2 only after a rebuilt installer (frozen build).

issues.observation: pc2 native_fault.log has 9 access violations; app.log shows the cascade signature: 'SystemError: ...QApplication::notify(): <built-in function perf_counter> returned a result with an exception set', "<class 'PySide6.QtWidgets.QMenu'> returned NULL without setting an exception", 'notify called with wrong argument types'. The trigger correlates with NETWORK failures during patient open (WinError 10065 'unreachable host' attachments, WinError 10060 timeouts). MULTI-STUDY FUNCTIONAL BEHAVIOUR IS HEALTHY: multistudy_rendered series_count=17 studies=3 / 16 studies=2 / 16 studies=3, sibling-study prefetch present, and the right_panel_cache_gate grew= decisions are correct (44 grew=1 are DIFFERENT patients' first opens with local_thumbs=0, then grew=0 cache hits — no refetch loop, no cross-patient, no missing study). study_enumerated_by_modality / cross_patient_skip / resync markers are ABSENT (this previous build predates the 2026-06-02 per-modality enumeration + resync work).
issues.whyMayBeWrong: The notify() override re-raises any event-dispatch exception into Qt's C++ caller by DESIGN (to capture a full traceback), but that converts a recoverable transient (a network blip raising during open) into a fatal SystemError/TypeError cascade across subsequent Qt calls. This is a crash-handling DESIGN choice, not a clear bug — do not silently change a safety/diagnostic mechanism.
issues.reasonForDeferral: Changing notify() to swallow-and-recover is a core-system change needing the author's sign-off (could mask real crashes / violates 'do not disable safety checks'). The conservative mitigation is to catch transient exceptions at their SOURCE in the open path (done for the overlay case in FIX-008) and to fix the upstream network failures (OBS-009). Several specific crash sites are ALREADY hardened in current source (loading_overlay liveness guard; tab-hover animations FIX-007) so they only reproduce on pc2's older build -> need a rebuilt installer.
issues.risk: medium (hard crashes during patient open when the server link is flaky).
issues.recommendedInvestigation: 1) Rebuild + reinstall on pc2 to pick up FIX-007/FIX-008 and the loading_overlay guard. 2) Fix that PC's PACS link (OBS-009). 3) DISCUSS with the author whether notify() should recover (log + return) for non-fatal exceptions instead of re-raising. 4) Separately verify the MPR axial-view (_mpr_views.py _create_axial_view) and add_patient_data crashes against current source — likely VTK/GPU-environmental and old-build line numbers respectively; not multi-study.

issues.observation: Patient 46370 (62 series, ALL local) opened in ~44s to first image (~100s total) on the live build, vs 1.5s for the same patient the day before. The main-thread stack sampler (viewer_diagnostics.log) showed the thread inside open()/fp_read()/os.path.exists() for the ENTIRE 42s gap; CPU ~1% and disk read ~50-180 KB/s (~69 ms/file) = I/O-WAIT-bound, not CPU/parse-bound. The FAST load re-reads every DICOM header off disk because a server-opened study (is_local=False) skips the DB-metadata path (H1); _build_metadata_headers_only read the headers SEQUENTIALLY on the main thread. The day-before fast open was because the study was mid-download (0 local series) so only a few files were read.
issues.whyMayBeWrong: Pure load-SPEED defect. The header reads are independent per file and file I/O releases the GIL, so on an I/O-bound disk they should overlap. Order/geometry/displayed result are unaffected (stubs are index-keyed and re-sorted + geometry-normalized regardless of read order).
issues.reasonForDeferral: n/a - fixed. Conservative + clinically output-preserving.
issues.resolution: FIXED (2026-06-15): added _read_header_stubs — an ADAPTIVE reader. It probes the first ~6 files; a fast SSD (parse-bound, <12 ms/file) stays SEQUENTIAL (honours the 2026-06-08 benchmark: a pool is ~2x slower there), while a slow/I-O-bound disk (>=12 ms/file) overlaps the remaining reads with a bounded ThreadPool (<=8 workers). Slow-disk micro-benchmark: 30 ms/file x60 -> 1.82s sequential vs 0.40s parallel (4.6x), byte-identical result. So 46370's ~42s scan drops to roughly ~9s. Gated by AIPACS_HEADER_SCAN_PARALLEL=auto(default)|0(legacy sequential)|1/force. The pattern matches an existing pydicom header-read ThreadPool already in this file (max_pydicom_workers). The concurrent server new-series check was ALREADY present and on by default (AIPACS_RESYNC_ON_REOPEN=1; _resync_patient_studies_from_server fire-and-forget, server fetch via asyncio.to_thread) — it had only appeared late because the 42s main-thread scan starved the qasync loop; with the scan fast it runs concurrently as designed.
issues.risk: low (load speed only; default-on auto path is identical to legacy on fast SSDs; flag-off forces legacy).
issues.relatedStudy: live patient 46370 (62 series local; ~69 ms/file slow disk)
issues.relatedTests: tests/code/viewer/test_header_scan_parallel.py (9 — completeness, index/order, mode-equivalence, failing-file, ordering invariant); tests/code/viewer/test_headers_only_parallel_scan.py (invariants, docstring updated)
issues.recommendedInvestigation: Remaining (larger, separate): the scan still BLOCKS the main thread (now ~9s not ~42s); fully de-blocking needs preview-first / off-thread load (deferred, render must stay on main thread). Also: a full 62-series re-download is queued on an ALREADY-complete study (wasteful, did not transfer) — fix the download-on-complete trigger. The proper H1 (use downloader-written DB metadata instead of re-reading headers) stays deferred until the downloader slice-spacing write-gap is fixed (clinical geometry). Best verified live: reopen 46370 and confirm first_series_visible drops + header_scan_parallel logs.

issues.observation: Full architecture review of the download->sync->open->preview->display lifecycle (2026-06-15). The pipeline already conforms to most standard client/server patterns: disk = source of truth for status, off-thread throttled resync-on-reopen (default on) that pulls only missing series, disk-count resume, atomic .part->replace writes, 5-layer download de-duplication, non-blocking open orchestration, cross-patient + multi-study guards, render coalescing. Gaps: P1 no unified local manifest (state spread across DM state store + dicom.db + download_progress.db + disk + ~6 memory caches; cross-layer updates not atomic); P2 the series LOAD still briefly blocks the UI thread (improved by FIX-009, not eliminated); P3 is_local=False for fully-downloaded server studies (H1); P4 a full re-download is queued even when the study is already complete (I/O contention); P5 sync granularity stops at series count (no SOP-level); P6 stale detection is manual (Settings button) not on-open; P7 drag-drop does not trigger download for a not-yet-local series; P8 no progressive Syncing/Stale/Failed UI surface.
issues.whyMayBeWrong: These are architecture/responsiveness/observability gaps, not output bugs. The implemented part (sync_manifest.py) is READ-ONLY (no writes, no downloads) so it cannot affect clinical output.
issues.reasonForDeferral: The structural fixes (S1-S6) each touch the clinical open/render or download-trigger path -> staged behind env flags + golden-compare per the safety rules; not changed unilaterally.
issues.resolution: DONE (review + safe foundation + S1): (1) the review document maps states/storage/transitions, the 6 scenarios, a standard-pattern scorecard, problems P1-P8, a KPI review, and a 10-item validation checklist; (2) NEW read-only sync_manifest.py = the unified local manifest + local-vs-server comparison (state vocabulary; missing_series/partial_series/missing_thumbnails/up_to_date), 11 unit tests, no DB needed, no writes; (3) IMPLEMENTED S1 + scenario-6 (P4 + 46640) flag AIPACS_OPEN_SKIP_DOWNLOAD_WHEN_COMPLETE (default on): the double-click open feeds the FRESH server series list to evaluate_sync and (a) SKIPS start_priority_download_immediately entirely when the server confirms nothing missing (download_skipped_complete), or (b) FILTERS the download queue to ONLY the missing/partial series (download_only_missing) when some are missing. Fixes BOTH the redundant re-download of a complete study (46370) AND the 46640 'all of them start downloading' case — a study that grew 1->11 on the server now queues the 10 NEW series, not all 11 (verified: 46640 open logged [FAST-SERIES-DOWNLOAD-QUEUE] series_count=11 for a 1-local/11-server study). DM resume is a 2nd layer; any error/unreachable-server -> full list; resync stays the safety net. LIVE-CONFIRMED 46370 after restart: first_series_visible 43912ms->1921ms (FIX-009) + download_skipped_complete + resync still ran server_series=62 changed=0. Guard tests test_open_skip_download_when_complete.py. STAGED (approval-gated, flag + golden-compare): S2 (scenario-5 stale behaviour ALREADY met by disk-first + FIX-004/005; remaining = auto-repair the lingering stale DB row + unify the duplicated comparison onto sync_manifest), S3 off-thread/preview-first load (the big responsiveness win), S4 drag-drop download trigger for a NEVER-downloaded series (common partial/downloading cases already handled by progressive-grow + open-time download; needs viewer->DM wiring + a real Qt drag to verify), S5 progressive UI, S6 SOP-level sync.
issues.risk: S1 is server-confirmed + falls through on doubt (no riskier than the existing disk-count resume); read-only model + doc carry no risk; the remaining staged items carry clinical-path risk and are gated.
issues.relatedStudy: live 46370 (re-download-on-complete + load block); clear-path consistency FIX-003/004/005/006
issues.recommendedInvestigation: Live-confirm S1: reopen a complete study, expect a 'download_skipped_complete' trace and NO '[FAST-SERIES-DOWNLOAD-QUEUE]' for it, and confirm a study with a genuinely new server series STILL downloads it (via the resync). Then S2/S3 as the next staged steps.

issues.area: Sync/DownloadManager (stale terminal state blocks new server series)
issues.observation: Patient 46640: uploaded 1 series, client downloaded it -> the Download Manager marked the STUDY state COMPLETED. The server then GAINED 10 more series. On reopen the download_diagnostics logged 'Download already exists (Status: Completed)' — R17 REJECTED the new download (allowed=False, action=skip) because check_study_complete=True against the STALE local number_of_series=1. So the 10 new series did NOT download via the normal open/resync path (both go through R17 / the queue dedup, both blocked by the COMPLETED state). The user only got them to download by forcing it (drag/manual), which then re-processed everything ('all of them start downloading').
issues.whyMayBeWrong: R17's COMPLETED de-dup is correct for a genuinely-complete study but is STALE once the study grows on the server. The completed state reflects the series count at download time, not the current server truth. Pure sync-correctness defect; no clinical-output change (it only governs WHEN/WHAT downloads).
issues.reasonForDeferral: n/a - fixed.
issues.resolution: FIXED (2026-06-15) flag AIPACS_OPEN_RESET_STALE_COMPLETE (default on), applied to BOTH server-grew paths: (1) the OPEN download wiring (_hp_patient_open) — when the fresh server list shows missing series it clears any stale TERMINAL (COMPLETED/CANCELLED) DM state via state_store.reset (the purpose-built force-redownload API) so R17 no longer rejects the new series; (2) the RESYNC growth path (_hp_series _resync_patient_studies_from_server) — when a study GROWS while being viewed, the same reset runs before dm.add_downloads so the queue de-dup ('Download already exists') doesn't block the new series (closes the grow-while-viewing residual gap). Only terminal/idle states are touched (no active worker to orphan); the resume scan still skips already-local files; combined with the download_only_missing filter (REVIEW-SYNC-001) the queue contains ONLY the new series, so already-local series do not re-download. Any error -> proceed unchanged. Guard tests test_open_skip_download_when_complete.py (open + resync).
issues.risk: low-medium: touches the DM state store from the open path, but only resets TERMINAL states (idle), is flag-gated, and falls through on error. Resume scan protects already-local files.
issues.relatedStudy: live 46640 (1 series local -> server grew to 11; 'Download already exists (Status: Completed)' at 16:36:26)
issues.recommendedInvestigation: Live-confirm after restart: open 46640 -> expect 'download_reset_stale_complete' + 'download_only_missing missing=10' + the 10 new series download while series already local is NOT re-downloaded. Longer-term: R17 should compare the completed state against the current server series count so the stale-complete case can't recur even without the open-path reset.

issues.area: Sync/Open (already-open patient not refreshed from server)
issues.observation: Patient 46533: opened with 6 series. Server then GAINED series. Single-clicking on the main page detected the growth (right_panel_cache_gate grew=1 -> new thumbnails shown on the main page), but double-clicking to open hit the early-return 'existing_tab_focused' path (the tab was still open from the first open), which just focuses the tab and RETURNS — it never re-checks the server, refreshes the viewer's series list, or downloads the new series. So the open viewer kept the old 6 series and the new ones neither showed nor downloaded (exactly the user report). The background resync also reported changed=0 because it compares DB series rows (already updated) not files, so it didn't recover it either.
issues.whyMayBeWrong: Re-open of an open tab is treated as a pure focus; the server-grew refresh is skipped. Sync-completeness defect; no clinical-output change (governs which series show/download, not how images render).
issues.reasonForDeferral: n/a - fixed.
issues.resolution: FIXED (2026-06-15) flag AIPACS_OPEN_REFRESH_ALREADY_OPEN (default on): when a double-click re-focuses an ALREADY-OPEN tab, after focusing it (kept instant) the open now (1) fires a FORCED resync (self._resync_patient_studies_from_server force=True) so any new server series are detected and DOWNLOADED (via FIX-010 stale-COMPLETED reset + download_only_missing), and (2) refreshes THIS viewer's series sidebar via existing_widget.set_server_series_info(fresh_server_series) — which is merge-aware, so only genuinely-new series are added (no reset of existing border/progress state). Both are best-effort, guarded, and run after the focus so they never block it. Guard test in test_open_skip_download_when_complete.py.
issues.risk: low-medium: adds a forced server check + a merge-aware viewer refresh on re-open; flag-gated; both wrapped in try/except and is_widget_alive-checked; focus stays instant.
issues.relatedStudy: live 46533 (opened 6 series; server grew; reopen hit existing_tab_focused with no refresh)
issues.recommendedInvestigation: Live-confirm after restart: open 46533, add series on the server, single-click (main page shows them), then double-click -> expect 'existing_tab_series_refreshed' + the new series appear in the open viewer AND download. FOLLOW-UP DONE (2026-06-15): the resync's 'changed=0 when DB has the rows but the files are missing' gap is closed — the resync is now disk-aware (flag AIPACS_RESYNC_DISK_AWARE, default on): it consults the manifest (disk files vs server) and treats disk-missing/partial series as a reason to sync, logging result=disk_missing + disk_missing=<list> in study_resync_check. Guard test test_resync_is_disk_aware.

issues.observation: Patient 46692: the app crashed and closed once after searching ALL modalities. No trace was captured (app.log had no crash cascade; native_fault.log stale 06/12) = a HARD native crash. The priority-flash on a thumbnail's progress border created BARE LOCAL QPropertyAnimation(widget.progress_border, b'_border_width') objects (no parent, no kept reference) and called start(); Python GC'd them while the 500 ms flash was still running, freeing the C++ object mid-flight -> access violation. An all-modality search renders many thumbnails and flashes many borders at once, so the race is hit. Same lifetime class as FIX-007/FIX-008.
issues.whyMayBeWrong: Classic PySide6 lifetime defect (a running QPropertyAnimation must stay referenced/parented). UI flash only; no clinical geometry/rendering involved.
issues.reasonForDeferral: n/a - fixed (clear SE/stability defect, output-preserving). STRONG candidate for the 46692 all-modality-search crash but not confirmable from a trace (hard crash, faulthandler stale); fixed regardless because it is a real latent crash of a known class.
issues.resolution: FIXED (2026-06-15): both flash animations are now parented to widget.progress_border AND keep a reference (widget.progress_border._priority_flash_anim / _priority_flash_anim2), so they can't be GC'd mid-flash. Identical visible flash. Guard test test_tab_hover_animation_lifetime.py::test_thumbnail_priority_flash_animation_is_parented_and_referenced.
issues.risk: medium (intermittent hard crash during thumbnail-heavy searches).
issues.recommendedInvestigation: If a crash recurs, capture the next native_fault.log dump to confirm the frame. Also note 46692's main-page thumbnail-staleness (#1): the right-panel cache gate used the stale stashed server count on single-click within the 5-min resync throttle, so new-series thumbnails didn't refresh until re-open (which now works via FIX-011, displayed thumbnail_count=5). Deliberate throttle; not changed.

issues.observation: On a client PC whose PACS backend runs MongoDB < 5.2, GetPatientList failed: 'Invalid $addFields :: caused by :: Unrecognized expression \$sortArray' (code 168, InvalidPipelineOperator). The backend aggregation uses $sortArray (unsupported pre-5.2), so the pipeline returns no patient data. The client's get_patient_list_safe sent ONE request and on failure just logged '❌ Patient list request failed' and returned None — no compatibility fallback. (Incident doc: docs uploads MONGODB_COMPATIBILITY_INCIDENT_2026-06-15.md.) ROOT CAUSE is server-side; $sortArray is NOT in this repo (confirmed) so the server backend is separate.
issues.whyMayBeWrong: Single-point dependency on an advanced MongoDB operator with no client degradation. Networking/availability, not clinical output.
issues.reasonForDeferral: n/a - fixed (client-side graceful degradation). The DEFINITIVE fix is server-side (drop $sortArray or upgrade MongoDB >= 5.2); the client fix only helps insofar as the server honours the degrade flags, but it never makes things worse (worst case it returns None, same as before, and the UI uses the local/cache path).
issues.resolution: FIXED (2026-06-15): get_patient_list_safe now degrades gracefully. Normal request first; ONLY on the specific $sortArray/InvalidPipelineOperator error (detected by _is_sortarray_compat_error — NOT timeouts/auth) it escalates: compatibility (compatibility_mode+mongodb_compatibility) -> simple (simple_query+no_sort) + client-side newest-first sort (_patient_list_client_sort; the home table re-sorts anyway). The first working mode is cached process-wide (_PATIENT_LIST_FALLBACK_MODE, lock-guarded) so later requests use one round-trip; a restart re-discovers (self-heals after a server upgrade). Config: socket_config.get_patient_list_fallback_mode() ('compatibility'|'simple') pins a mode; is_force_compatibility_mode() starts in compatibility; config/socket_config.json adds patient_list_fallback_mode=null + force_compatibility_mode=false (safe defaults = unchanged behaviour). A healthy/modern server is UNAFFECTED (normal path succeeds; fallback inert). 8 unit tests (fake send_request).
issues.risk: low: healthy servers unchanged (fallback only triggers on the exact $sortArray error); non-$sortArray failures are not degraded; total failure returns None as before.
issues.recommendedInvestigation: PRIMARY: fix the server — drop $sortArray (use $sort / sort in app code) or upgrade MongoDB to >= 5.2. Confirm the backend actually honours compatibility_mode/simple_query/no_sort (the client fallback assumes it does); if it ignores them, only a server fix or the local-cache path will populate the list. For the known-legacy client set force_compatibility_mode=true (and optionally patient_list_fallback_mode='compatibility').

issues.area: Sync/DownloadManager (R17 stale-COMPLETED hardening — close at source)
issues.observation: Root closure of the stale-COMPLETED class (FIX-010/FIX-011): R17b (DB duplicate check) ALREADY verified files on disk before trusting a 'Completed' status and allowed re-download when files were missing — but R17a (the in-memory StateStore check) blanket-BLOCKED any COMPLETED study without a disk check. So once a study's in-memory state was COMPLETED, a server-grew/files-cleared study was rejected at the de-dup rule itself. FIX-010 patched the two real entry paths (open + resync) by resetting the stale state before R17; this closes it at the rule so ANY enqueue path is covered.
issues.whyMayBeWrong: Inconsistency between R17a (no disk check) and R17b (disk check). De-dup correctness, not clinical output.
issues.reasonForDeferral: n/a - fixed.
issues.resolution: FIXED (2026-06-15) flag AIPACS_R17_DISK_AWARE_COMPLETED (default on): R17a now mirrors R17b via a shared _task_files_complete_on_disk(task) helper — a COMPLETED study whose task series are NOT all present on disk (dir missing or dcm_count < image_count) is allowed to RESUME (action='resume', should_resume=True) instead of being blocked; a genuinely-complete study still blocks (action='skip', no re-download). CANCELLED still always blocks (respect the user's cancel). The helper returns True (trust completed -> block) when there is nothing to verify or on any error, so it can only ALLOW a re-download when files are provably missing (worst case = a resume-protected re-download, never data loss). Plugin mirror synced (sync_plugin_mirrors.py). Guard tests test_r17_disk_aware_completed.py (8); 150 download_manager tests still green.
issues.risk: low-medium: core de-dup rule, but the change only converts the COMPLETED-but-files-missing case from block->resume; genuinely-complete and CANCELLED unchanged; flag-gated; falls through to block on error; the resume scan skips already-local files.
issues.relatedStudy: 46640 / 46533 (server-grew studies blocked by stale COMPLETED state)
issues.recommendedInvestigation: Live-confirm: a study whose in-memory state is COMPLETED and then grows on the server should now download the new series even without an explicit open/resync reset.

issues.area: Sync (server contentVersion fast-gate — cheapest authoritative staleness signal)
issues.observation: The server (STUDY_STORAGE_AND_VERSIONING) maintains a monotonic per-study contentVersion, $inc'd on ANY content change, and returns it on GetStudyThumbnails. Before this, every reselect-resync did the DB series-count query + disk manifest scan even when nothing had changed on the server — work with no cheap short-circuit. There was no client use of the server's own change signal.
issues.whyMayBeWrong: Pure efficiency + correctness-of-skip: the disk-aware resync was correct but unconditionally expensive; the cheapest correct gate (server change counter) was unused.
issues.reasonForDeferral: n/a - implemented.
issues.resolution: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-15) flag AIPACS_CONTENT_VERSION_SYNC (default on). Capture: content_version is surfaced from the GetStudyThumbnails response into study_info at three additive points (socket get_study_thumbnails, the gRPC mapper series_utils, and get_series_info_from_server) — all None-safe/inert when the server omits it. Store: new content_version_store.py persists per-study the contentVersion at which the local copy was LAST CONFIRMED COMPLETE on disk (JSON under USER_DATA_ROOT, in-memory cache, atomic write, fail-open). Gate (resync): server_cv == local_synced => skip the DB query + disk scan entirely (trace result='current_cv'); server_cv higher/unknown => fall through to the existing disk-aware manifest check; the synced version is stamped ONLY on the confirmed-complete (not needs_sync) branch, never on mere enqueue (recording an un-downloaded version would pin an incomplete study as current). A forced/manual refresh (force=True) NEVER cheap-skips. Clear-on-delete: delete_patient_completely forgets the stored version so a cleared study re-syncs. Disk stays the source of truth; contentVersion only decides whether to look.
issues.risk: low: additive capture (inert if field absent), gated default-on but identical to disk-aware-only when the server omits contentVersion; the skip can only fire when server==last-confirmed-complete (and never on a forced refresh); the stale-after-clear hole is closed by the clear() wire; all writes fail-open. No clinical-output path touched.
issues.recommendedInvestigation: Live-confirm against a server that returns content_version: download_diagnostics study_resync_check should log result='current_cv' (cheap skip) on the second reselect of an unchanged study, and fall through to grew/disk_missing exactly once when the server version advances. If the production server does NOT yet return content_version, the gate stays inert (disk-aware behaviour unchanged) — coordinate with the server team to confirm GetStudyThumbnails carries the field.

issues.area: FAST viewer window/level (heterogeneous series render near-black — CSI spectroscopy)
issues.observation: Patient 46370 series 61 (csi3d_se_prostate, Siemens CSI spectroscopy) opened near-black in our FAST viewer while another workstation showed it fine. The series is HETEROGENEOUS: SPECTRUM secondary-capture frames (512x512, values 0-4067, own WC2048/WW4096) interleaved with REFERENCEIMAGE MR frames (640x600, values 0-413, own WC301/WW637). The viewer seeds the series window from slice 0 (a SPECTRUM frame -> WW4096/WL2048) and keeps it across slices; under a 4096-wide window the reference frames (max 413) map to near-black. Confirmed by rendering Instance_0002 with WW4096 (near-black) vs its own WC301/WW637 (clear prostate axial — matches the other workstation). pixel_array decodes fine; not a load/decode failure. The per-instance WC/WW was already available (get_default_window_level(idx) returns it) but the stack-scroll path (_set_slice_impl) never re-applied it.
issues.whyMayBeWrong: Clinical-render: a diagnostic frame is unviewable at the wrong window. The fix touches the W/L pipeline (clinically sensitive) so it is surgical + flag-gated + bounded to substantial differences.
issues.reasonForDeferral: n/a - fixed (flag-gated, default on, no-op for normal series).
issues.resolution: FIXED (2026-06-15) flag AIPACS_FAST_PER_INSTANCE_WINDOW (default on). On stack scroll, when the user has NOT set a custom window AND the slice's own DICOM WC/WW differs SUBSTANTIALLY from what's displayed (_window_differs_substantially: width ratio >= 1.5x or level shift >= 0.5*width), re-apply the slice's own window via the existing apply_default_window_level (which is scroll-cache-guarded). Normal homogeneous series (and series with only MINOR per-slice WC/WW variation) keep a stable window while scrolling -> byte-identical to legacy. Manual W/L still persists across slices (gated on flag_set_custom_window_level). `0` restores legacy series-constant window.
issues.risk: low-medium (clinical render, hence the guards): only fires on a DRAMATIC per-slice window difference (heterogeneous/spectroscopy), never for normal or minor-variation series; manual W/L unaffected; flag-gated and instantly revertible. 251 fast/stack-drag tests green + new per-instance-window guards. NOT yet live-verified (running app has old code + remote-session focus block) — restart required to load the fix; the corrected render is proven by the offscreen WC301/WW637 vs WW4096 comparison.
issues.recommendedInvestigation: After restart: open 46370 series 61 and scroll — the REFERENCEIMAGE frames (prostate + CSI grid) should render at their own WC301/WW637 instead of near-black, while normal MR series (e.g. 46423) keep stable windowing while scrolling. NOTE: this fixes the IMAGE frames; rendering the spectra as an analysis PLOT (Cho/Cr/Ci over ppm, as the other workstation does on the SPECTRUM frames) is a separate, larger spectroscopy-rendering feature, not in scope here.

issues.area: Socket client robustness (download failures on a client PC — 'pc user 2 sanam' logs)
issues.observation: Client-PC download_diagnostics (previous version) showed two real recurring download failures: (A) UnicodeDecodeError 'utf-8 codec can't decode byte 0xe7/0xf6/0xed/0xfb' at socket_client.py:838 `json.loads(response_data.decode('utf-8'))` (5x) — a non-UTF-8 byte (Persian/Western-European name/description encoded Windows-1256/Latin-1) in the response aborts the ENTIRE download. The identical strict decode existed in modules/network/socket_client.py:241 (patient-list/thumbnail parse). (B) NetworkError 'Too many broadcast messages, no response received' on GetSeriesImages (43x) — the broadcast-skip loop capped at a hard max_broadcast_retries=10; on a busy multi-workstation PACS the server interleaves >10 legitimate `type='broadcast'` events before the client's response, failing the download. (Also ~96x benign GetReportStatus timeouts/'Invalid response length header' — report-status polling flakiness, same as the live razi server; not a crash, left as-is. And 7x 'Download cancelled (preemption)' = expected viewer-drag preempt.)
issues.whyMayBeWrong: Both A and B are real client-side defects causing failed downloads (not env). A is a hard crash on valid-but-non-UTF-8 field data; B is too-low a tolerance for normal server broadcast traffic.
issues.reasonForDeferral: n/a - fixed.
issues.resolution: FIXED (2026-06-15). (A) New _decode_socket_payload() decodes strict UTF-8 first (normal case, zero change) then falls back to UTF-8 with errors='replace' so json.loads still succeeds and the download proceeds — only the offending text field degrades to a placeholder, image data untouched. Applied at the download parse site and (inline, same logic) at the patient-list/thumbnail parse site. (B) max_broadcast_retries is now _MAX_BROADCAST_RETRIES = max(10, env AIPACS_MAX_BROADCAST_RETRIES default 50) — raised from a hard 10; safe because each recv is socket-timeout-bounded (a genuinely lost response still fails, just after more skips) and the skipped messages are confirmed valid broadcasts, not a stream desync. Mirror synced; 156 download_manager tests green incl. 6 new guards.
issues.risk: low: (A) tolerant decode is identical to strict on valid UTF-8 (the normal path) and can only PREVENT a crash; (B) only raises a skip cap (no busy-loop — bounded by socket timeout) and is env-revertible to 10. No clinical-render path touched.
issues.relatedStudy: client PC 'pc user 2 sanam' (Persian edition); patients incl. KHAZAIE ZIVAR
issues.recommendedInvestigation: On the client PC after update: GetSeriesImages downloads of patients with non-ASCII names should no longer abort with UnicodeDecodeError, and 'Too many broadcast messages' failures should drop sharply. If broadcast failures persist at 50, investigate WHY the server broadcasts so heavily during downloads (server-side) rather than raising the cap further. The GetReportStatus timeouts are a separate, benign server-side report-endpoint issue.

issues.area: Voice note recording — short/quick recordings silently saved nothing (client PC 'pc user 3 vahid')
issues.function: VoiceWidget._on_stop_internal (+ first logger in this module)
issues.observation: User report: saving a patient voice note as an attachment often failed and the user had to record 2-3 times. The client logs contained ZERO voice/audio traces because the whole voice path reported errors only via QMessageBox, never the logger. Code analysis found the root cause: the sounddevice callback (_callback_capture) puts captured frames into a queue (_audio_q); a 60 ms QTimer (_on_timer) is the ONLY thing that moves them into _audio_frames, which is what gets written to the .wav. On stop, _on_stop_internal stopped the timer and then saved WITHOUT draining the queue — so every recording lost its tail, and a SHORT recording (shorter than a tick, or when the timer was starved by a busy UI/disk) lost ALL its frames, leaving _audio_frames empty so `if self._audio_frames:` was False and the save was a SILENT no-op (no file, no message, no log). Intermittent by nature -> 'record 2-3 times until it sticks'. (The native_fault.log on this PC is an unrelated download-subprocess multiprocessing-spawn access violation at download_process_worker.py:148, dated 6/11.)
issues.whyMayBeWrong: Real data-loss defect in the capture pipeline (audio captured but discarded), made invisible by a silent save path and no logging. Not env/mic-specific — the queue tail is always dropped; short clips lose everything.
issues.reasonForDeferral: n/a - fixed.
issues.resolution: FIXED (2026-06-15): _on_stop_internal now DRAINS _audio_q into _audio_frames before the save (after stopping the stream+timer; the queue is recreated per take, so it only ever drains the current recording). Added the module's first logger: success logs frames/drained/samples/duration/path; a save exception logs the traceback (still shows the existing QMessageBox); and the no-audio case logs a WARNING instead of being a silent no-op. Both save routes (popup Save and inline F9 Save+Sync) go through _on_stop_internal, so all are covered. voice_tool_ui.py is not plugin-mirrored.
issues.risk: low: the drain only APPENDS frames that were already captured (cannot corrupt or lose data); for a normal recording it adds the final <=60 ms tail; logging is additive. No clinical-image path touched.
issues.relatedTests: tests/code/system/test_voice_queue_drain_on_stop.py (4: short-take saved, tail included, empty-take logged, source order) + existing voice/shortcut suites (17 green)
issues.recommendedInvestigation: After update: short voice notes should save reliably on the first try, and app.log will now carry [VOICE] traces (frames/duration on success, a WARNING when a take captured no samples) so any remaining mic/device problem is diagnosable instead of silent.

issues.area: App crash hardening — QApplication.notify() malformed dispatch (client PC 'pc user 3 vahid')
issues.observation: app.log.3 logged a CRITICAL unhandled exception: 'PySide6.QtWidgets.QApplication.notify() called with wrong argument types: notify(QEvent, QEvent)' at main.py notify(), via aipacs.crash.notify -> _aipacs_excepthook (UNHANDLED EXCEPTION, will propagate to Qt). The notify override calls super().notify(receiver, event) and, on any exception, logs an H10 snapshot then re-raises (correct, so REAL handler crashes surface). But here super().notify itself raised TypeError because `receiver` was a non-QObject (a QEvent) — a malformed/spurious dispatch (no code in the repo calls app.notify with wrong args; all other .notify() are the unrelated notification inbox, so this is a Qt/teardown/native-plugin edge case). Re-raising a spurious dispatch crashed the app.
issues.whyMayBeWrong: A spurious malformed dispatch should not crash the workstation; the re-raise is meant for genuine handler exceptions, not for super().notify rejecting bad arguments.
issues.reasonForDeferral: n/a - fixed.
issues.resolution: FIXED (2026-06-15): the except path now detects the malformed case (the exception isa TypeError AND receiver is NOT a QObject) and returns False (event treated as unhandled) instead of re-raising. The happy path (return super().notify(receiver, event)) is byte-identical, and EVERY genuine handler exception (receiver IS a QObject) still hits the existing H10-snapshot capture + re-raise, so real crashes are still surfaced. QObject is imported locally inside the (rare) except path, so the hot path is untouched.
issues.risk: low: change is confined to the exception path; normal event dispatch unchanged; only a provably-malformed (non-QObject receiver) TypeError is swallowed (returning 'unhandled'), which is strictly safer than crashing. Guard tests pin the invariant.
issues.relatedStudy: client PC 'pc user 3 vahid' (1 occurrence, app.log.3)
issues.recommendedInvestigation: If the warning 'notify() skipped malformed dispatch' ever recurs frequently, capture the surrounding events to identify which native plugin / teardown path issues the bad notify call. As a single rare event it is now non-fatal.

issues.area: Mode-aware synchronization — separate Live-Server from Local/Offline/Import/CD workflows
issues.function: WorkflowMode / resolve_workflow_mode / requires_live_server_sync / requires_remote_resync / local_is_source_of_truth / missing_files_trigger_server_download / log_mode_decision; _resync_patient_studies_from_server gate
issues.observation: Per the mode-separation directive: the client must clearly distinguish live-server workflows (server is source of truth; version-aware sync mandatory) from local/offline ones (local is source of truth; live server must never be required), and must not mix the two. The mode (SourceOfPatientLoad = SERVER/DB/IMPORT/OFFLINE_CLOUD; CD burn is a separate local action) WAS represented but checked ad-hoc with DIFFERENT source-sets at every site (`==DB`, `!=DB`, `(DB,OFFLINE_CLOUD)`, p2 LOCAL_GUARD `(DB,OFFLINE_CLOUD,IMPORT)`, a one-off `==IMPORT` resync guard) — hidden assumptions that invite cross-mode bugs. In particular the AUTO contentVersion resync ran for EVERY source, so an Import/CD/local patient would auto-contact the live server.
issues.whyMayBeWrong: Mixed online/offline assumptions are a correctness + reliability risk: a local/import/CD patient must not be forced to verify against (or be blocked by) the live server, and must not be marked stale when the server is down; a live-server patient must always version-check + sync.
issues.reasonForDeferral: n/a - implemented (core); remaining ad-hoc sites migrate incrementally (the doc is the guard).
issues.resolution: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-15): new pure-logic policy module sync_mode_policy.py is the SINGLE source of truth — WorkflowMode {LiveServer, LocalDatabase, Import, OfflineServer, CDBurn, Unknown}, resolve_workflow_mode(source), and named predicates (requires_live_server_sync, requires_remote_resync, requires_server_version_check, local_is_source_of_truth, can_trust_local_cache_as_authoritative, missing_files_trigger_server_download) + log_mode_decision (mode/source-of-truth/local+server version/skip-reason; no credentials). Contract: LiveServer treats the server as truth + runs strict version-aware sync (the existing contentVersion + disk-aware manifest); LocalDatabase is a locally-cached SERVER study so it ALSO runs the contentVersion sync (default on — synchronization contract, STUDY_STORAGE_AND_VERSIONING §4.3/§7) while local DB/disk stays the DISPLAY truth; OfflineServer keeps its cloud sync; Import/CD/Unknown never auto-contact the server. The AUTO resync now gates on requires_remote_resync (LiveServer + OfflineServer + LocalDatabase run; Import/CD/Unknown skip) and logs the mode on both skip and run; a manual 'Refresh / Sync from server' (force=True) always runs for any source. CORRECTION (post audit vs server spec): the LocalDatabase default was briefly set OFF, which REGRESSED contentVersion sync for downloaded patients — reverted to ON (AIPACS_LOCALDB_AUTO_SERVER_SYNC=0 for strict local-only). Full per-mode contract + validation checklist in docs/architecture/SYNC_MODE_SEPARATION.md.
issues.risk: low: the policy is additive/behaviour-preserving for LiveServer, LocalDatabase, and OfflineServer (all keep their contentVersion/cloud sync — NO regression). The ONLY intentional behaviour change is that the auto resync no longer fires for Import / CD / Unknown sources — those studies are not on the server (no contentVersion), so the call was a wasteful no-op; a manual refresh still works for any source. No clinical-render path touched.
issues.relatedStudy: architecture directive (Live vs Local/Offline mode separation) + STUDY_STORAGE_AND_VERSIONING server spec; relates to FIX-015 (contentVersion), the p2 LOCAL_GUARD, 45611
issues.recommendedInvestigation: Verify against the server spec: a DB/Local patient whose server contentVersion advanced (new instances, attachment, voice, capture, or document) should detect server_cv>local_cv on reselect and pull the delta (download_diagnostics study_resync_check). Import/CD patients must NOT auto-contact the server. Next: migrate the remaining ad-hoc source checks (_hp_patient_open is_local, _hp_series cache gates, the p2 LOCAL_GUARD) to the policy predicates so every site is consistent + logged.

issues.area: pc user 3 vahid log sweep — classification of the remaining signatures
issues.observation: Full error sweep of the client logs (508 ERRORs in download_diagnostics, plus app/viewer). Classified: (1) ~408 GetReportStatus failures ('No response' / 'timed out' / 'Invalid response length header' / WinError established-connection) = the benign report-status polling flakiness seen on every client + the live server; high VOLUME but not a crash. (2) GetSeriesImages 'Too many broadcast messages' / 'Did not receive endpoint response (broadcasts=38, timeout=30s)' = the broadcast-flood download failure ALREADY fixed by FIX-018 (cap raised 10->50; the 38-broadcast case is now covered). (3) GetStudyInfo timed out (21) = the known unsupported-endpoint probe (ZETA §14, single fast attempt + TTL skip-cache); expected, low impact. (4) qasync '_thumbnail_task_cleanup' callback exception (5) = ALREADY RESOLVED in current source (the cleanup is now a trivial guarded method that no longer chains into on_plus_button_clicked/show_patient_studies). (5) notify(QEvent,QEvent) CRITICAL = FIX-020. (6) _vc_load/_vc_switch 'Error loading series [WinError 3] path not found' + 'change_series async load FAILED' (1+3) = the cross-study/missing-files series-path class (partially guarded by series8_45033 work); low frequency here. (7) progressive-fast STALE-EXHAUSTED (1) = graceful give-up after 5 retries, expected. (8) EchoMind Secretary 'Phase 1 LLM call failed: Network error contacting RAZI' (1) = environment/proxy (no internet to the LLM API). (9) native_fault.log = a download-subprocess multiprocessing-spawn access violation (reduction.dump -> popen_spawn_win32 -> download_process_worker.py:148), dated 6/11 — a separate, rare worker-spawn crash worth a dedicated look if it recurs.
issues.whyMayBeWrong: Most are benign/env/already-fixed; the two worth tracking are the series-path-not-found load failures (clinical-adjacent) and the download-subprocess spawn AV.
issues.reasonForDeferral: Items 1/3/7/8 benign or env; 2/4/5 already fixed (FIX-018 / current source / FIX-020); 6 and 9 are low-frequency and need a live repro before a targeted change.
issues.resolution: Documented. No further blind change. Recommend: keep the GetReportStatus polling on the server-side radar (volume); if the download-subprocess spawn AV (native_fault) recurs, investigate what object is being pickled into the worker Process (download_process_worker.py:148) — a non-picklable/native handle is the usual cause.
issues.risk: n/a
issues.recommendedInvestigation: Item 6 (series path-not-found) and item 9 (worker-spawn AV) — capture a live repro before changing code. The rest are benign, env, or already fixed.
